name: Sodium bicarbonate
executiveSummary: HCO₃⁻. Acute acidosis: estimate **mEq = (desired HCO₃ − actual) × 0.3 × kg**. Orient. bolus **1–2 mEq/kg** diluted IV. NICU/selected arrest: **1–2 mEq/kg** slow. Always treat the cause; correct hypokalemia first.
indications:
## Indications

- Selected severe metabolic acidosis; specific intoxications; refractory hyperK (regimens).
- NRP: restricted use (not routine in arrest).

## Precautions

- Extravasation → necrosis. Na⁺ load. Alkalosis, hypocalcemia.
- **Incompatible with calcium, magnesium, and atropine** in-line.

> Ampule 1 M = **1 mEq/mL** (8.4%). Peripheral: dilute (e.g. 1/6).

adulto.dose: Selected situations: **1–2 mEq/kg** IV; or calculate **(desired − actual) × 0.3 × kg**. Infuse slowly (often >2 h if not emergency).
adulto.administration: Diluted IV; central line for high concentrations. Peripheral: dilute (e.g. to **0.5 mEq/mL**).

pediatrico.presentation: IV solution 1 M (1 mEq/mL); PO 10% compounded ~1.2 mEq/mL; caps 1 g ~ 12 mEq.
pediatrico.dose: Acute IV: **mEq = (desired − actual) × 0.3 × kg** (orient. bolus **1–2 mEq/kg**). Chronic PO: factor **0.6 × kg**.
pediatrico.finalConcentration: Diluted peripheral; central up to 1 mEq/mL slow push.
pediatrico.infusionRate: Usual infusion 4–8 h via pump if not emergency.

neonatal.dose: **1–2 mEq/kg** slow IV in selected severe acidosis / NRP when indicated — not routine in arrest.
neonatal.notes: IVH risk if rapid bolus — neonatology.

stability:
## Stability

- Room temperature. Discard remainder of opened ampule. Do not mix with Ca²⁺.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Necrosis from extravasation, alkalosis, hypernatremia, hypocalcemia, flatulence (PO).

bibliography.citation: AHA / NRP — bicarbonate not routine in cardiac arrest.
